validated_results.title: Soy and isoflavone consumption in relation to prostate cancer risk in China.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Original case-control study reporting a dietary genistein intake estimate for incident prostate cancer risk.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of genistein intake
extraction.population: Men aged 50 to 89 years in China

effect_size.excerpt: There were also statistically significant associations comparing the highest quartile of intake of soy foods (OR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.28-0.95) and genistein (OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.29-0.97) with the lowest quartiles. There was also an indication of a reduced risk associated with intake of daidzein (OR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.31-1.04 for the highest versus lowest quartile).

confidence_interval.excerpt: There were also statistically significant associations comparing the highest quartile of intake of soy foods (OR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.28-0.95) and genistein (OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.29-0.97) with the lowest quartiles.

validated_results.title: Incidence of cancer and mortality following alpha-tocopherol and beta-carotene supplementation: a postintervention follow-up.
validated_results.reason: Postintervention follow-up of a randomized supplementation trial reporting alpha-tocopherol (vitamin E) and incident prostate cancer.

sample_size.excerpt: Postintervention follow-up assessment of cancer incidence and cause-specific mortality (6 years [May 1, 1993-April 30, 1999]) and total mortality (8 years [May 1, 1993-April 30, 2001]) of 25 563 men.

cases.excerpt: For prostate cancer incidence (n = 672), the RR was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.76-1.03) for participants receiving alpha-tocopherol compared with nonrecipients.

effect_size.excerpt: Overall posttrial relative risk (RR) for lung cancer incidence (n = 1037) was 1.06 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.94-1.20) among recipients of beta-carotene compared with nonrecipients. For prostate cancer incidence (n = 672), the RR was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.76-1.03) for participants receiving alpha-tocopherol compared with nonrecipients.
